```{r include=FALSE}
### call libraries
library(easypackages)
libraries("tidyverse","foreign","lubridate","reshape2", "ggplot2","RColorBrewer","knitr","forcats","openxlsx","statar","svDialogs","xlsx", "magrittr","stringr", "data.table","janitor","kableExtra","leaflet", "readr", "rmarkdown","rowr", "gganimate", "gifski","tidycensus","sf","htmltools","acs","tigris","mapview","rgeos", "ggrepel", "censusxy","gdata","lavaan","mclust","tmap", "raster","rgeos","gmapsdistance","viridis","cowplot","lintr","leaflet.extras","censusapi","data.table","gridGraphics","readxl","haven","ggridges","extrafont","extrafontdb","datamodelr","Lahman","DiagrammeR","fs","readxl","rsvg","V8","tidylog","distill","tidylog")
```

```{r include=FALSE}
### pull in data from raw excel files; each tab in each excel file will be a separate dataframe
read_excel_allsheets <- function(filename) { 
  sheets <- readxl::excel_sheets(filename) 
  x <- lapply(sheets, function(X) readxl::read_excel(filename, sheet = X)) 
  names(x) <- sheets 
  x 
} 

### create list of all files we want -- all .xlsx files in project data folder
mi_placement_data <- list.files(path = "C:\\Users\\abyrum\\The Council of State Governments\\JC Research - Documents\\JC Research - JJ_Michigan - JJ_Michigan\\Data\\Raw\\MDHHS\\Placements\\", 
                     pattern = "*Placements.xlsx",
                     full.names = TRUE)

### lapply function over list of files we want to import
list_of_mi_placement_tabs <- lapply(mi_placement_data, read_excel_allsheets)

### assign names from iowa_files to list_of_ticket_dataframes
names(list_of_mi_placement_tabs) <- janitor::make_clean_names(basename(mi_placement_data))

### convert lists to tibbles -- we still have lists of lists, though
list2env(list_of_mi_placement_tabs, envir=.GlobalEnv) 

### convert list to separate dataframes with clean names
names(placements_xlsx) <- janitor::make_clean_names(names(placements_xlsx))

list2env(placements_xlsx,envir=.GlobalEnv) 

### remove original list of dataframes from environment
rm(list=ls(pattern="placements_xlsx"))
```

```{r include=FALSE}
### join all files together using data table diagram as visual guide using left join, starting with child_details -- our base demo file

###### de-dup child_details using PERSON_ID
child_details %<>%
  distinct(PERSON_ID,.keep_all = TRUE) ### file already unique by PERSON_ID; no records dropped 

###### de-dup placements using all columns
placements %<>%
  distinct(.,.keep_all = TRUE) ### file already unique; no pure duplicates and no records dropped 

### inner join placements to child_details -- dropping records from child_details with no matching placement data
child_details_placements <- inner_join(child_details, placements, by = "PERSON_ID")

### IGNORE incidents FOR NOW -- NEED TO CLEAN + PIVOT WIDE BEFORE MERGING; MAY NEED TO ANALYZE SEPARATELY -- NOT JOINED TO MAIN ANALYTIC FILE AS I NEED TO EXPLORE HOW AND IF WE CAN JOIN INCIDENTS TO SPECIFIC PLACEMENTS + CASES

# ###### de-dup incidents using all columns
# incidents %<>%
#   distinct(.,.keep_all = TRUE) ### file already unique; no pure duplicates and no records dropped 
# 
# ### join incidents to child_details_placements
# child_details_placements_incidents <- left_join(child_details_placements, incidents, by = c("PERSON_ID","PROVIDER_ID"))

### IGNORE legal_status FOR NOW -- NEED TO CLEAN + PIVOT WIDE BEFORE MERGING; MAY NEED TO ANALYZE SEPARATELY -- NOT JOINED TO MAIN ANALYTIC FILE AS I NEED TO EXPLORE HOW AND IF WE CAN JOIN legal_status TO SPECIFIC PLACEMENTS + CASES

# ###### de-dup legal_status using all columns
# legal_status %<>%
#   distinct(.,.keep_all = TRUE) ### file already unique; no pure duplicates and no records dropped 
# 
# ### join legal_status to child_details_placements_incidents
# child_details_placements_incidents_legal <- left_join(child_details_placements_incidents, legal_status, by = "PERSON_ID")

###### de-dup case_plans using all columns
case_plans %<>%
  distinct(.,.keep_all = TRUE) ### file already unique; no pure duplicates and no records dropped 

###### de-dup offenses using all columns
offenses %<>%
  distinct(.,.keep_all = TRUE) ### file already unique; no pure duplicates and no records dropped 

### join offense to case_plans to attach MiSACWIS CASE ID to each offense; joining separately from jj_assessments as we have to de-dup differently in each scenario; right join to keep all offenses records and only records from case_plans which match -- but prefer to have case_plans records as first columns (so right join)
case_plans_offense <- right_join(case_plans,offenses,by = c("PERSON_ID","MiSACWIS_CASE_ID")) %>% 
  distinct(PERSON_ID,MiSACWIS_CASE_ID,CHARGED_OFFENSE_DATE,CHARGED_OFFENSE,FINAL_OFFENSE_MCL_CODE,.keep_all = TRUE) %>% ### offenses are duplicated over CASE_PLAN_ID since we're joining on c("PERSON_ID","MiSACWIS_CASE_ID"); de-dup to keep one unique charge per PERSON_ID/MiSACWIS_CASE_ID
  dplyr::select(-c(CASE_PLAN_ID,PLAN_DATE,PLAN_TYPE)) %>% ### only merging with case_plans to join offense data to misacwis id
  group_by(PERSON_ID,MiSACWIS_CASE_ID) %>% ### pivot wide by PERSON_ID,MiSACWIS_CASE_ID (spreading charge data wide)
  mutate(col_name=paste0("charge_num",'_',row_number())) %>%
  ungroup() %>% 
  pivot_wider(id_cols = c(PERSON_ID,MiSACWIS_CASE_ID), names_from = col_name, values_from = CHARGED_OFFENSE_DATE:REFERRING_OFFENSE_IND, values_fill = NA) %>% 
  dplyr::select(where(~!all(is.na(.x))))

### join case_plans_offense to child_details_placements_incidents_legal
child_details_placements_offense <- left_join(child_details_placements, case_plans_offense, by = "PERSON_ID")

###### de-dup jj_assessments using all columns
jj_assessments %<>%
  distinct(.,.keep_all = TRUE) ### file already unique; no pure duplicates and no records dropped 

### join jj_assessments and case_plans first to remove unnecessary records (most of the case plan records -- which just state multiple different case plan for each case, but no further detail); right join to keep all jj_assessments records and only records from case_plans which match -- but prefer to have case_plans records as first columns (so right join)
case_plans_jj <- right_join(case_plans,jj_assessments, by = c("PERSON_ID","CASE_PLAN_ID","PLAN_TYPE","PLAN_DATE")) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(RISK_LEVEL)==TRUE) ### drop all records with missing risk level data; these are records that had a case plan entry but no jj_assessment or offense data attached to that case plan record (for our purposes, these case plan records are not necessary)

### join jj_assessments to child_details_placements_incidents_legal_case; using full join as not all columns from case_plan will match, but we don't want duplicate column names
child_details_placements_offense_assess <- full_join(child_details_placements_offense, case_plans_jj, by = c("PERSON_ID","MiSACWIS_CASE_ID"))

### IGNORE ACADEMIC EVALUATIONS FOR NOW -- NEED TO CLEAN + PIVOT WIDE BEFORE MERGING

###### de-dup academic_evaluations using all columns
# academic_evaluations %<>%
#   distinct(.,.keep_all = TRUE) ### file already unique; no pure duplicates and no records dropped 
# 
# ### join academic_evaluations to child_details_placements_incidents_legal_offense_assess
# child_details_placements_offense_assess_acad <- left_join(child_details_placements_offense_assess, academic_evaluations, by = c("PERSON_ID"))
```

```{r include=FALSE}
### clean dates, create race/ethnicity var with both four and six values, and create sex flag
child_details_placements_offense_assess_clean <- child_details_placements_offense_assess %>% 
  clean_names() %>% 
  mutate(birth_dt = ymd(birth_dt),
         plan_date = ymd(plan_date),
         eff_begin_date = ymd(eff_begin_date),
         eff_end_date = ymd(eff_end_date),
         placement_begin_date = ymd(placement_begin_date),
         placement_end_date = ymd(placement_end_date),
         placement_begin_date_year = year(placement_begin_date),
         placement_end_date_year = year(placement_end_date),
         age_placement_start = time_length(difftime(placement_begin_date, birth_dt), "years"),
         race_csg_4 = case_when(
    multi_race=="Black/African American" & hispanic_latino_ind!="YES" ~ 1,
    hispanic_latino_ind=="YES" ~ 2,
    multi_race=="White" & hispanic_latino_ind!="YES" ~ 3,
    multi_race %in% c("American Indian/Alaskan Native","American Indian/Alaskan Native, Native Hawaiian/Other Pacific Islander","Asian","Black/African American, American Indian/Alaskan Native","Black/African American, Asian","Black/African American, Native Hawaiian/Other Pacific Islander","Native Hawaiian/Other Pacific Islander","Unable to Determine","Unknown","White, American Indian/Alaskan Native","White, Asian","White, Black/African American","White, Black/African American, American Indian/Alaskan Native","White, Black/African American, Asian","White, Black/African American, Native Hawaiian/Other Pacific Islander","White, Native Hawaiian/Other Pacific Islander") & hispanic_latino_ind!="YES" ~ 4,
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA)),
    race_csg_4 = factor(race_csg_4,
         levels = c(1,2,3,4),
         labels = c("Black", "Hispanic", "White", "Other"))) %>%  ### use factor function to assign labels to values
  mutate(gender_clean = case_when(
    gender_txt=="Female" ~ 1,
    gender_txt=="Male" ~ 2,
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA)),
    gender_clean = factor(gender_clean,
         levels = c(1,2),
         labels = c("Female", "Male"))) ### use factor function to assign labels to values

### clean dates, create race/ethnicity var with both four and six values, and create sex flag for demo/placement file only
child_details_placements_clean <- child_details_placements %>% 
  clean_names() %>% 
  mutate(birth_dt = ymd(birth_dt),
         placement_begin_date = ymd(placement_begin_date),
         placement_end_date = ymd(placement_end_date),
         placement_begin_date_year = year(placement_begin_date),
         placement_end_date_year = year(placement_end_date),
         age_placement_start = time_length(difftime(placement_begin_date, birth_dt), "years"),
         race_csg_4 = case_when(
    multi_race=="Black/African American" & hispanic_latino_ind!="YES" ~ 1,
    hispanic_latino_ind=="YES" ~ 2,
    multi_race=="White" & hispanic_latino_ind!="YES" ~ 3,
    multi_race %in% c("American Indian/Alaskan Native","American Indian/Alaskan Native, Native Hawaiian/Other Pacific Islander","Asian","Black/African American, American Indian/Alaskan Native","Black/African American, Asian","Black/African American, Native Hawaiian/Other Pacific Islander","Native Hawaiian/Other Pacific Islander","Unable to Determine","Unknown","White, American Indian/Alaskan Native","White, Asian","White, Black/African American","White, Black/African American, American Indian/Alaskan Native","White, Black/African American, Asian","White, Black/African American, Native Hawaiian/Other Pacific Islander","White, Native Hawaiian/Other Pacific Islander") & hispanic_latino_ind!="YES" ~ 4,
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA)),
    race_csg_4 = factor(race_csg_4,
         levels = c(1,2,3,4),
         labels = c("Black", "Hispanic", "White", "Other"))) %>%  ### use factor function to assign labels to values
  mutate(gender_clean = case_when(
    gender_txt=="Female" ~ 1,
    gender_txt=="Male" ~ 2,
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA)),
    gender_clean = factor(gender_clean,
         levels = c(1,2),
         labels = c("Female", "Male"))) ### use factor function to assign labels to values
```

## Missing Data in 'jj_assessments' File/Excel Tab

* 4,326/5695 youth in 'child_details' file/Excel tab have no record in 'jj_assessments' data (76% of youth in child_details have no jj_assessments data) 
* There are only 1,369 unique youth in 'jj_assessments' data (24% of 'child_details')
* Output below illustrates match rate between 'child_details' and 'jj_assessments' where 'x' represents 'child_details' table. Rows only in 'x' are records in 'child_details' with no corresponding records in 'jj_assessments' table -- by joining on "PERSON_ID"

### Joining 'jj_assessments' to 'child_details'
```{r warning=FALSE}
### inner join placements to child_details
child_details_assessments <- inner_join(child_details, jj_assessments, by = "PERSON_ID")
```

<br>

## Missing Data in 'placements' File/Excel Tab

* 704/5695 unique youth in 'child_details' file/Excel tab have no placement data (12% of youth in child_details have no placements data) 
* There are only 4,991 unique youth in 'placements' data (88% of 'child_details')
* Output below illustrates match rate between 'child_details' and 'placements' where 'x' represents 'child_details' table. Rows only in 'x' are records in 'child_details' with no corresponding records in 'placements' table -- by joining on "PERSON_ID"

### Joining 'placements' to 'child_details'

```{r warning=FALSE}
### inner join placements to child_details 
child_details_placements <- inner_join(child_details, placements, by = "PERSON_ID")
```
